Let pi(K)=K.g and S(G)=pack(G). On the tested valid three-concept graph, unpack(S(G))=G preserves concept ids, words and CSR edges. The composite Kb::new(unpack(S(pi(K)))) discards K's assertions, additional layers and extra edges. Its preimage includes all admitted K states sharing G; the snapshot alone cannot recover a learned or layer-specific answer. Property specificity and layer visibility were observed only after explicit synthetic assertions were supplied.

Let V(G)=store::check(G). V checks array lengths, offsets and reference/string bounds; unpack separately checks encoded enum discriminants. V does not impose in(v)={(r,u): (u,r,v) in out}. A three-concept graph with a mismatched but in-bounds incoming edge passes V and pack/unpack, while ancestors follows outgoing edges. Therefore V=Ok excludes tested structural corruption but admits relational inconsistencies; it is not a certificate of complete graph semantics.

kg Id(h,l)=(h<<32)|l is injective over two u32 components. With equal l and distinct h, the tested identifiers remain distinct through edge sort, flags filter and column persistence; a reopening of the temporary registry retains both keys. onto Cid is an index into a particular graph and has no implemented identity-preserving conversion from Id. Dropping h identifies distinct vertices; any future adapter must supply namespace and provenance explicitly.

forward: Reject an invalid source first, then the first invalid endpoint in row/edge order. On valid graphs return None exactly at unreachable vertices and Some of the minimum walk weight elsewhere, unless a source-reachable negative cycle exists, which returns ReachableNegativeCycle. All signed i64 edge weights, duplicates, loops and disconnected components are supported. i128 checked addition returns DistanceOverflow if representation fails; on current <=64-bit usize targets at most V edges per synchronous round fit i128.

inverse: Let X be allocated finite adjacency vectors with i64 weights and usize sources, and Y the typed Result<Vec<Option<i128>>,BellmanFordError> observation space, excluding allocation failure and nontermination. Let R subset X times Y be the graph of the Forward relation including source-before-edge validation and first checked-overflow precedence. Define U=X times Y and behavior_complement=U minus R. Thus every input has its unique permitted observation in R; all other typed observations are in the complement. The shortest-walk characterization assumes representable synchronous sums (guaranteed on current <=64-bit usize targets). Given successful vector d, compatible antecedents are all validated graphs and valid sources whose reachable minimum walk weights equal d and have no reachable negative cycle. InvalidSource recovers source>=V; InvalidEdge recovers a valid source and first offending edge; ReachableNegativeCycle recovers existence and source reachability, not its unique vertices. nodes.description: counting_sort exact implementation
forward: For empty input return Ok unchanged. Otherwise span=max-min+1: overflow returns RangeOverflow; span above budget returns BucketLimitExceeded; fallible histogram reserve failure returns AllocationFailed. Each error preserves input. Success returns the unique ascending permutation with the same multiplicities.
inverse: Within observations (input, budget, allocator outcome, Result, output slice), exclude changed input on Err, changed length or multiplicity, nonascending success, success past a range/budget failure, and error variants inconsistent with validation precedence. This is a source-derived relation, not just negative fixtures.

A successful sorted output admits every input permutation of that multiset, with budget at least its inclusive span and successful reserve; empty output admits empty input and any budget. Errors admit unchanged input with matching overflow, budget or allocation branch. Original order is generally not recoverable.
For successful sorting S, S(S(x))=S(x). Translation by a constant preserving usize bounds preserves order and span. Tests check idempotence and the narrow span at usize::MAX.

For a fixed ascending y and successful allocation, S(x,b)=y iff H(x)=H(y) and b>=span(y), with empty input needing zero buckets. All distinct permutations survive; support alone is insufficient. Oracle histogram_fibers_retain_multiplicity_not_order enumerates 256 four-place inputs and finds 12 predecessors of [2,2,4,5].

For strictly increasing f on the finite input support with every image representable, S(f(x),b2)=f(S(x,b1)) when both allocations succeed and budgets cover their respective inclusive spans. A nonlinear or affine map may change the required budget. Wrapping arithmetic violates the premise. The checked affine map 3v+11 and insufficient transformed budget are tested.

For nonempty x with representable span s, successful budget antecedents are b>=s conditional on successful allocation; b<s yields precisely BucketLimitExceeded{s,b} unchanged. This is an upper ray, independent of input length. Repeated singleton-valued inputs need one bucket. The test scans budgets 0 through 6 at span 3.

Validation partitions calls in order: empty succeeds; unrepresentable inclusive span yields RangeOverflow regardless of budget; otherwise s>b yields BucketLimitExceeded; otherwise reserve failure yields AllocationFailed; otherwise success. All error fibers retain original order because no writes precede reserve. Capacity overflow is deterministic evidence; physical allocator exhaustion is untested.

After counting, H[j] equals multiplicity of min+j. Reconstruction writes disjoint intervals [sum_{i<j}H[i],sum_{i<=j}H[i]) with min+j. These intervals partition [0,n), including empty buckets; histogram zeros do not remove gaps from the resource span. Replacing min+j by min preserves length but violates values and histogram, rejected by the compiled mutant.

nodes.description: extended_gcd exact std-only implementation
forward: Define E(a,b) by the Euclidean recurrence with initial remainder rows (a,1,0),(b,0,1), updating (r,s,t),(r1,s1,t1) to (r1,s1,t1),(r%r1,s-q*s1,t-q*t1), q=floor(r/r1). Return the first row when r1=0; explicitly E(0,0)=(0,0,0). This fixes deterministic coefficients, rather than admitting every Bezout solution.
inverse: In U of input pairs and candidate triples, U minus graph(E) contains wrong gcds, violated integer Bezout identities and coefficient triples unequal to the deterministic Euclidean result even if their identity holds. This exact recurrence target has finite correspondence evidence, not a formal Rust proof.

Given (g,x,y), reconstruct all u64 pairs (a,b) satisfying E(a,b)=(g,x,y). Necessarily ax+by=g and gcd(a,b)=g, but those conditions alone do not enforce the coefficient policy. For g=0 only (0,0) with x=y=0 qualifies; (g,1,0) for g>0 can admit several b. Preserve the recurrence constraint and ambiguity.

For (a,b)!=(0,0), let E(a,b)=(g,x0,y0). All integer solutions to ax+by=g are exactly x=x0+k*(b/g), y=y0-k*(a/g), k in Z. This describes certificate solutions, not the graph of the deterministic coefficient policy: only k=0 is returned. For (0,0), every integer coefficient pair solves the equation but only (0,0) is returned. Arbitrary k and products require mathematical integers or checked arithmetic; i128 is not a universal family domain.

For g>0, positive d divides both a and b iff d divides g. Thus g is the greatest common divisor in the divisibility order and ax+by=c has an integer solution iff g divides c. Sufficiency scales the returned certificate by c/g; necessity follows by divisibility of every linear combination. At (0,0), only c=0 is solvable, and every positive d divides both inputs; no finite positive maximum exists.

For modulus m>=2 and a:u64, gcd(a,m)=1 iff a has an inverse modulo m. The unique representative r in [0,m) is E(a,m).x rem_euclid m. Other Bezout solutions project to the same r. No inverse is inferred when gcd>1; modulus zero is undefined and modulus one is excluded. For verification convert a,r,m to u128: a*r fits u128 for u64 operands; the same product may overflow i128 even though the signed coefficient identity is safe.
limitations: Partial syntax omits macro expansion and semantics; bounded tests are not a proof.
No executable approximate profile attached; this algorithm is exact.

forward: For length below two return Ok unchanged. Otherwise reserve n scratch values before writes; reserve failure returns TryReserveError with unchanged input. Eight stable byte passes in increasing significance yield the unique ascending permutation, preserving all multiplicities.

Given successful sorted output y, compatible original inputs are all permutations of its multiset; allocation must succeed unless len<2. Err admits the unchanged input and failed reserve. For an internal digit-pass result, predecessors are shuffles of digit subsequences preserving order within each digit. Sorting is not injective; no unique original ordering is claimed.

S(S(x))=S(x). Each byte pass preserves every digit subsequence. Tests use distinct scalar values sharing selected byte keys to observe internal pass stability; scalar full-sort equality cannot demonstrate attached payload stability.

For fixed byte b and digit-sorted y, P_b(x)=y iff for every digit d the subsequence of x with digit d equals that of y in order. Thus predecessors are interleavings of fixed digit subsequences, not arbitrary multiset permutations. Distinct values [0x300,0x100,0x201,0x001] give six accepted shuffles at byte zero; reversing a same-digit pair is rejected.

After k stable passes in increasing byte significance, output is the stable ordering of original input by its low 8k bits. At k=8 this is full unsigned order; using a full-width mask avoids shifting by 64. Reversing pass order or reversing equal-digit source subsequences invalidates the inductive step. All eight stages are compared against an independent stable key sort.

S(f(x))=f(S(x)) for f strictly increasing on the finite support with representable u64 images and successful allocations. The checked affine map 257v+19 is observed; wrapping addition on [0,MAX] is a countermodel when representability is dropped. This is a full-sort law, not a law that byte partitions commute with arbitrary relabeling.

Lengths zero and one succeed without reservation. For n>=2 the sole fallible reservation precedes every pass and copy; Err therefore has unchanged input and a failed reservation as compatible antecedent. Scratch length and requested capacity are n u64 elements (the allocator may reserve more) and counts use 256 usize slots per pass. No public budget parameter or allocator failure injection exists; exact allocator feasibility cannot be inferred from n alone.

Counts sum to n and prefix starts partition destination into digit intervals [sum_{e<d}H[e],sum_{e<=d}H[e]). Left-to-right source traversal advances each cursor once per occurrence, preserving its subsequence. Disjoint intervals imply no dropped or duplicated values. nodes.description: aho_corasick exact implementation
forward: Build an owned trie with breadth-first failure links and inherited sorted output IDs. Scan arbitrary bytes and emit every exact occurrence, including overlaps, in (end,pattern) order. Duplicates preserve IDs; empty patterns match all boundaries.

Trie labels are distinct prefixes; each nonroot failure points to a shorter proper suffix prefix. BFS initializes failure ancestors first. Sorted output IDs exactly match suffix patterns, including empty IDs once. State is longest prefix suffix of consumed text.
inverse: Exclude missing or spurious occurrences, duplicate reports of the same (end,pattern), out-of-range offsets, wrong byte spans, changed inputs, and an output not ordered by (end,pattern). Empty-pattern omissions and deduplication of equal pattern values are outside the contract.

For fixed patterns P and length n, restrict R to valid pattern IDs and ranges 0<=s<=e<=n, unique (end,pattern) pairs, and canonical increasing (end,pattern) order. Such an output R admits exactly byte texts T of length n for which each (i,s,e) in R has e-s=|P_i| and T[s..e]=P_i, and every matching span is in R. These positive and negative span constraints generally admit several texts; no unique reconstruction is claimed.

After consuming T[..e], state represents the longest suffix of T[..e] which is a trie prefix. Compatible histories are precisely histories with this longest-prefix-suffix property, not histories with only the same final byte.
Outputs at a state are exactly IDs whose patterns are suffixes of that state's trie label. Each pattern ID occurs once; distinct IDs with equal bytes coexist. Root outputs are exactly empty IDs.
Every injective byte map applied jointly to patterns and text preserves the entire match list. Noninjective maps can introduce occurrences and are excluded.
Permuting pattern IDs transports each report's pattern field by the same permutation, then sorting by (end,pattern) restores required order. Repeated byte patterns remain separate IDs.
For text U followed by V, filtering matches on UV to end<=|U| gives exactly matches on U, including empty matches at the shared boundary only once.
With e empty pattern IDs and text length n, empty reports number e(n+1); all other reports have start<end. No patterns yields an empty result on every text.

nodes.description: suffix_array exact implementation
forward: Return the unique permutation of offsets 0..n whose nonempty suffixes increase lexicographically by unsigned byte order. Prefix-doubling pairs refine ranks until distinct; exclude the empty suffix.

Ranks encode equal truncated prefixes and their lexicographic order. Each offset appears once; absent second ranks sort before actual ranks. Unique ranks imply complete suffix order. Index addition is checked.
inverse: Exclude omitted, repeated or out-of-range offsets, the empty suffix n, or adjacent offsets whose suffixes are in descending order. Input bytes remain unchanged.

For a fixed permutation A of 0..n, compatible byte texts are precisely length-n texts whose adjacent suffixes T[A[j]..] are strictly lexicographically increasing. Several texts satisfy these constraints; A alone does not recover bytes.

Observe rank ordering and equality, not the initial literal numeric byte ranks. At width k, equal ranks mean equal length-k truncated suffix prefixes and rank order matches their lexicographic order. Any byte text with the same ordered prefix equivalence classes is compatible with this rank observation.
Sorting pairs (rank_i, optional rank_{i+k}) orders length-2k truncated prefixes; None is less than every present rank. Assigning consecutive ranks preserves pair equality and strict ordering.
A strictly increasing map on the input byte support preserves the suffix array. Injectivity without monotonicity is insufficient, and wrapping maps violate the premise.
Prepending a byte strictly below every input byte produces array [0] followed by every original offset increased by one. The empty input gives [0].
For n=3, output [2,1,0] admits exactly nonincreasing triples; over three byte values there are ten compatible triples. Equal-value and strictly decreasing texts can yield the same suffix order.

Each round doubles represented prefix length unless all n ranks are unique and returns. Width>=n distinguishes suffix lengths even for constant bytes. checked_add handles absent tails; saturating doubling cannot prevent termination for valid byte slices.

nodes.description: weighted_interval_scheduling exact classical dynamic programming implementation
forward: Reject first original index with start>=end. Sort by (end,start,index). For item j let p be count of earlier ends<=start. B(j+1)=max(B(j),B(p)+weight). Take only strict improvements, then reconstruct original indices in chronological order.

A successful (indices,total) admits all valid item arrays whose deterministic recurrence chooses those indices with that sum. Endpoints can shift while preserving compatibility. Weights of excluded items may vary while remaining dominated. Neither input nor unique optimum follows from output.

Half-open positive-duration intervals are compatible exactly when one end<=the other's start. Positive duration ensures sorted predecessor candidates precede the current item; replacing <= by < loses adjacency.

At equal candidate and previous score, skip current sorted item. Duplicate intervals select earliest original index if positive. Zero weights never create a strict gain. This witness rule does not promise lexicographically minimal original-index vectors.

Uniform endpoint translation preserving i64 bounds preserves order, compatibility and exact Schedule. Multiplying all weights by positive integer preserving u64/u128 bounds preserves chosen indices and scales score; zero multiplier does not preserve witness.
Input permutation preserves optimum weight, but indices transform and equal-key ties may pick a different original item. Thus only score invariance is unconditional.

Err InvalidInterval{i} admits arrays with all earlier start<end and item i start>=end; later items unconstrained. After validation, DimensionOverflow precedes allocations; checked WeightOverflow occurs during DP. On usual 32/64-bit targets the latter two are unreachable for valid allocated non-ZST Item slices; allocator exhaustion is not caught.

metamorphic_relation: Positive integral scaling k with representable images multiplies squared distance by k² and preserves indices; k=0 collapses all points and need not preserve indices.

duplicate_fiber: Zero distance iff equal coordinates. Sorted (point,index) runs start with the smallest two indices of each run. Minimum over adjacent equal-point pairs selects the globally least pair. All-equal input returns (0,1,0) without recursion.

A strip of width 2delta and height delta partitions in each half into constant many cells of diameter <delta; hence constant many candidates per point, even with boundary ties. Re-sorting strips gives T(n)=2T(n/2)+O(n log n), O(n log²n); sequential recursion peaks at O(n) vectors.

nodes.description: prime_factorization exact std-only implementation
forward: F(0)=Err(ZeroInput). For 1<=n<=u64::MAX, F(n)=Ok([(p1,e1),...,(pk,ek)]) with strictly increasing primes, positive exponents, and product p_i^e_i=n. The empty product gives F(1)=Ok([]). Fundamental unique factorization makes this mathematical target single-valued.
inverse: Over the stated input/output universe, U minus graph(F) excludes nonzero errors, accepted zero, composite bases, unsorted or duplicate primes, zero exponents, and any product unequal to n. Product equality alone is insufficient, as [(4,1),(3,1)] at n=12 shows.

For a canonical factor vector v, the unique compatible input is its mathematical product if <=u64::MAX, including empty v ->1. Noncanonical vectors have empty preimages. Err(ZeroInput) reconstructs exactly 0. Unlike general lossy outputs, this complete canonical output is injective.
For positive a,b with a*b<=u64::MAX, v_p(a*b)=v_p(a)+v_p(b) for every prime p; merge sorted factor vectors by adding exponents. No machine-overflow product is admitted.
For prime p and e>=1 with p^e<=u64::MAX, F(p^e)=[(p,e)]. Zero is rejected and one has empty support. Composite bases must first be factored.
For positive a,b, a divides b iff every prime exponent of a is <= the corresponding exponent of b, absent primes having exponent zero. This relates factorization to divisibility, including one.
Sorted distinct prime bases, positive exponents and checked exact product equal to n certify the entire canonical output by unique factorization; product alone fails to exclude composite bases.

For positive n with factor vector (p,e), the number of positive divisors is product(e+1); distinct prime count is vector length. Products here are mathematical integers; any optional machine projection requires checked arithmetic.
For remaining>1 with no prime divisor below d and d>remaining/d, remaining is prime. Equality must still be tested: d*d=remaining at prime squares. This condition avoids forming overflowing d*d.
limitations: Finite observations are not universal proof.

nodes.description: chinese_remainder exact std-only implementation
forward: Preflight the entire list for the first zero modulus and return ZeroModulus{index}. Otherwise fold from (0,1). For current (a,m) and normalized next (b,n), set g=gcd(m,n). If g does not divide b-a, return None. Otherwise L=m*(n/g); if L>u64::MAX return ModulusOverflow. Let t=(((b-a)/g) * inverse(m/g modulo n/g)) modulo n/g, using the Bezout coefficient of m for gcd(m,n). Return updated ((a+m*t) modulo L,L), eventually Some. Modulus one uses the sole zero residue. This operational error policy is part of the target.
inverse: U minus graph(S) excludes unnormalized Some, wrong LCM or wrong solution class, None for compatible reached prefix, accepting a zero modulus, wrong first zero index, and an overflow not selected by the left-to-right policy. Mathematical unsatisfiability of the entire list alone does not force None when an earlier merge overflows.

For Some(r,M), all compatible input lists whose total LCM is M and whose intersection is r+M*Z reconstruct the output, with r<M and M>0. Many lists fit: [(8,18)] and [(2,6),(8,9)]. Prefix LCM divides final M, hence no overflow occurs for these valid lists. Error and None preimages additionally obey the preflight and first terminal prefix policy; they do not uniquely recover inputs.
For Some(r,M), integer solutions are exactly x=r+k*M for k in Z. This family uses mathematical integers; no arbitrary machine multiplication is implied.

Two positive-modulus constraints intersect iff their residue difference is divisible by gcd(m,n). For a successful list, output satisfies every input and output modulus equals LCM, jointly certifying equality of solution classes rather than mere membership.

On positive-modulus lists whose total mathematical LCM fits u64, permutations preserve Some or None. Outside this domain, overflow can precede a contradiction in one order and follow it in another. Zero error indices also change under permutation.

Replacing an input residue by any u64 value congruent modulo its positive modulus preserves output. All Some residues are canonical in [0,M). Residue addition must remain within u64 when used as a machine transformation.

nodes.description: a_star original exact algorithm
forward: Validate start then goal, heuristic length, zero goal heuristic, all endpoints, then all edge inequalities h(u)<=w(u,v)+h(v). On admitted inputs A* orders snapshots by (g+h,g,vertex), discards stale distances and strictly relaxes edges. Return the first fresh goal pop with its predecessor chain; exhaustion means unreachable.
inverse: Within the declared input/result universe, excluded transitions include accepting a failed validation, incorrect first-error payloads, returning a non-realizable or nonminimal path, a cyclic witness, None for a reachable goal, and wrapped arithmetic. This is a source-derived inner description of semantic nonbehavior, not an empirical complement of sampled outcomes.

For a distance-only observation d, candidate antecedents are every admitted graph/start/goal/heuristic with a realizing path of cost d and no cheaper path; None has precisely unreachable-goal antecedents. For a full Path observation additionally require the deterministic heap/strict-parent trace to select those vertices. Omitting this trace is explicitly an outer reconstruction approximation. Errors recover inputs with exactly the first failing check. Self-loop changes and multiple consistent heuristics give nonunique fibers.

For every admitted arc define reduced cost w+h(v)-h(u)>=0 in mathematical integers. A start-to-v path has reduced sum g+h(v)-h(start), so the A* priority differs from reduced distance by the fixed constant h(start). This explains settlement; it does not admit merely guessed heuristic values.

On a fixed graph/start/goal every two admitted heuristic vectors produce the same distance or None. Their witness paths may differ because heap order changes. Zero heuristic is always admitted after endpoint validation and recovers Dijkstra distance semantics.

A returned vertex list begins at start, ends at goal, contains no repeated vertex and traverses actual arcs. With parallel arcs the minimum capacity-free edge weight between successive vertices sums to the returned distance. forward: Reject doubled variable-count overflow then first out-of-range literal in clause order, left before right. Encode negative literal 2v, positive 2v+1; each (a OR b) adds NOT a -> b and NOT b -> a. For output Some(a), compatible formulas on |a| variables satisfy every clause under a and have the canonical SCC/condensation rank inequalities selecting exactly a. The satisfaction condition alone is an outer preimage approximation, since some satisfying assignments are not selected. None corresponds to formulas with a variable and its negation mutually reachable. Error preimages recover count overflow or the first invalid literal position and payload. Duplicate clauses supply distinct full-output antecedents.

If a variable and its negation lie in one SCC there are implication paths in both directions. Each satisfying valuation must preserve truth along implications, so either truth choice contradicts the opposite endpoint. This is a mathematical certificate relation; the API returns None without exposing the actual paths.

The SCC helper sorts components by minimum vertex, not topological order. Map every implication through its component owner, omit self arcs, preserve duplicates, and obtain topological ranks through the existing DAG helper. Assignment correctness depends on this wiring; SCC child correctness alone does not establish the solver.

Permuting or duplicating clauses preserves the implication reachability and canonical SCCs. Condensation arc multiplicity/order cannot alter smallest-ready-vertex topological choice, hence the exact assignment is unchanged. Validation errors are excluded from this relation because clause indices and first-fault ordering can change.

Complementing any chosen subset of variable polarities maps satisfying assignments bijectively by flipping the same bits. Satisfiability is invariant. The solver's selected assignment need not transform identically, because numeric component tie breaking is not equivariant; only the transformed witness's feasibility is asserted.

Adding clauses can only remove satisfying valuations. Unsatisfiability is upward closed under valid clause additions. A newly returned assignment, if any, satisfies the old formula; assignment identity is not preserved in general.

Zero variables with no clauses yields the empty assignment; variables with no clauses are all true under the canonical numeric rank tie rule. A repeated literal is a unit clause. Opposite unit clauses force None. Tautologies impose no truth constraint, though a deterministic selected witness remains governed by ranks.

nodes.description: stoer_wagner original exact algorithm
forward: Validate all row lengths then upper-triangle symmetry. Run maximum-adjacency phases over active supervertices, selecting greatest accumulated connection with smallest original survivor ID as tie breaker. The last selected supervertex defines a phase cut; compare weight then oriented sorted side with previous phase cuts. Merge its weights and original-vertex group into the penultimate vertex. Return the best phase cut.
inverse: In the declared input/result universe exclude acceptance of a nonsquare/asymmetric matrix, wrong first error, a trivial or unsorted cut side, a side excluding vertex zero, a weight unequal to original crossing capacity, a suboptimal objective, and wrapped sums. This is a source-derived semantic exclusion model rather than an enumerated negative-test set.

For a full Cut(w,S), candidate antecedents are square symmetric nonnegative matrices where S is sorted, proper, contains zero, has crossing sum w and no cut has lower weight. Those constraints form an outer reconstruction relation: exact antecedents additionally require the deterministic phase sequence and equal-phase tie rule to select S. Every diagonal is free, giving explicit nonunique full-output fibers. None has all valid matrices of size zero or one as preimages.

Given the active partition P, quotient capacity W[A,B]=sum of original capacities across A and B. Merging A and B replaces each external capacity by W[A,C]+W[B,C]. Every quotient cut lifts to a union of original groups with exactly equal weight; cuts separating A from B are intentionally lost and accounted for by the phase theorem.

The stored last-supervertex group is nonempty and proper at every phase. Sorting it and complementing when it excludes zero preserve cut weight in a symmetric matrix. Summing original rows across the returned side independently certifies feasibility and objective value, though minimum optimality needs exhaustive cuts or the phase theorem.

Increasing one or more undirected capacities cannot reduce global minimum cut value, since each candidate partition sum is nondecreasing. Positive integer scaling multiplies the minimum value and preserves all capacity-order comparisons when representable in the input type. Cut witness identity under arbitrary increases is not promised.

Simultaneously permuting rows and columns preserves the minimum value and maps every feasible cut to an equal-weight cut. The chosen side need not follow the permutation because survivor tie order and zero orientation change; the API makes no global lexicographic minimum-side promise.

Arbitrary diagonal changes leave every cut sum, phase connection, merge to an external group and returned result unchanged. This exact discarded-coordinate relation supplies recoverable crossing data without claiming recovery of loop capacities.

All nonsquare-row errors precede asymmetry errors; first bad row or lexicographic upper-triangle pair determines the payload. u64 inputs are nonnegative by construction. Checked u128 merge/connection sums cannot wrap; finite tests cross u64::MAX but do not exercise actual u128 overflow or allocation failure.

nodes.description: lcp_array exact byte algorithm
forward: For finite byte text T of length n, return (A,L): A sorts the nonempty suffixes, L[0]=0 if n>0, and L[r]=max k with T[A[r-1]..A[r-1]+k]=T[A[r]..A[r]+k]. Empty input returns two empty vectors.

A is a permutation of 0..n; rank[A[r]]=r. The carried prefix is a lower bound for the next comparison after subtracting one. All comparisons obey common<n-start and common<n-previous, bounding additions by n-1.
inverse: Within U = finite input texts paired with arbitrary vector pairs, absent behaviors include unequal output lengths, nonpermutation A, L[0]!=0, and any adjacent L value differing from direct byte-prefix equality. This is a source-derived inner characterization of excluded outputs under successful allocation.

For fixed (A,L), retain every length-n byte text whose suffix order is A and whose adjacent common-prefix lengths are L. The fiber is usually non-singleton: ([1,0],[0,1]) admits every equal-byte pair, including three pairs over {0,1,2}. Order/LCP do not recover byte labels.

Fix suffix order A. The inverse-rank vector is uniquely rank[A[r]]=r; an inconsistent rank is excluded. Fix rank without T and the compatible inputs remain all texts inducing that suffix order; rank does not supply byte identity.

At each start with positive rank, common is a lower bound on LCP with its lexicographic predecessor. After measuring h, the next candidate starts at max(h-1,0); encountering the least suffix resets the bound. This relies on suffix-order predecessor constraints, not arbitrary permutations.

For fixed ranks a<b, LCP(T[A[a]..],T[A[b]..]) = min L[a+1..=b]. The interval is nonempty and the suffix order must correspond to this exact text; swapping a suffix array from another text invalidates the premise.

A strictly increasing byte map on the observed alphabet preserves both A and L. Injective decreasing maps preserve equality lengths only for a fixed pair of offsets, not the ordered arrays; noninjective maps can lengthen prefixes.

For fixed n and L, the number of distinct nonempty substrings is n(n+1)/2 - sum L. This mathematical integer identity is tested with explicit substring sets at n=5; API does not perform the potentially overflowing product.
For n equal bytes, A=[n-1,...,0] and L=[0,1,...,n-1]. For n=0 both vectors are empty. Long constant fixtures exercise maximal carried prefixes and finite suffix bounds.

nodes.description: burrows_wheeler exact byte algorithm
forward: Sort all n cyclic rotations lexicographically with equal rotations ordered by ascending source offset. Return their last bytes C and the row p whose source offset is zero. Empty T returns ([],0). Inverse checks p then computes an LF candidate and accepts it iff its canonical transform equals (C,p).

Every doubling order is a permutation. Ranks identify and order cyclic prefixes of the current width; pair sorting doubles width. shifted avoids overflowing i+width. Final (rank,offset) sorting makes periodic ties deterministic. LF maps each byte occurrence to the same ordered occurrence in the sorted first column.
inverse: In the universe of text/result pairs, exclude altered byte multiplicities, wrong sorted-rotation last columns, and noncanonical primary rows. Inverse rejects out-of-range p before any reachability check, and rejects unreachable in-range (C,p) pairs. Source-derived excluded behavior is not a semantic proof.

The full canonical pair (C,p) has exactly one input text when reachable, recovered by inverse; otherwise the fiber is empty. Projection to C alone retains ambiguity: abab and baba both produce bbaa, with primary rows 0 and 2. Neither column-only reconstruction nor accepting every LF cycle recovers the original.

Equal rotations of a periodic text are ordered by original offset. If the least cyclic period is d (so d divides n), each equal-rotation class has n/d members; source offset zero is first in its class. For bbaa only primary 0 or 2 is canonical; 1 and 3 are rejected despite decoding periodic candidates.

LF(i)=number of column bytes less than C[i] plus count of equal bytes strictly before i. Stable occurrence numbering gives a permutation; equal symbols alone do not identify which occurrence was meant. Following LF n times from p reconstructs a candidate, not reachability certification.

At width w<n, sorting (rank[i],rank[(i+w) mod n]) refines cyclic prefixes to length 2w. Once width reaches n, order of those prefixes agrees with full rotations, including equality. Saturating doubling cannot stall before reaching valid slice length n.

For a strictly increasing map f of byte support, transform(f(T))=(f(C),p). Sorting equivalence and stable tie offsets survive; mere injectivity without byte-order preservation does not preserve row order.

For n=0, p=0 is the sole valid metadata and decodes empty. For n>0, p>=n gives InvalidPrimaryIndex. For remaining metadata, canonical retransformation equality chooses Ok(candidate) versus InvalidTransform. These precedence partitions cover every byte column and usize primary.

For each byte b, count_b(T)=count_b(C), since predecessor offsets form a permutation. This necessary condition does not certify a valid encoded pair. The inverse finite search oracle enumerates all possible input texts separately.

nodes.description: wildcard_matching exact byte algorithm
forward: Return true iff the complete pattern consumes the complete text. A literal byte consumes the same byte, '?' consumes one arbitrary byte, and '*' consumes k>=0 arbitrary bytes. There is no escaping or Unicode decoding. The frontier stores exact prefix-language membership.

Before updating cell j+1, diagonal is the old row[j], above is old row[j+1], and row[j] is current-prefix membership. A star accepts left OR above; a nonstar accepts diagonal AND byte predicate. Initial row accepts exactly all-star pattern prefixes.
inverse: Within U of finite (text,pattern,bool) observations, exclude true when no whole-string token consumption exists and false when one exists. Anchoring forbids an interior literal match by itself. Bytes outside '?' and '*' remain literal, including backslash; Unicode scalar or path-separator semantics are absent.

For fixed pattern P and result true, the fiber is exactly its byte language L(P); for false it is the complement within finite byte strings. Many distinct texts match '*'. A Boolean and pattern cannot recover a unique original text or its allocation history.

At text prefix length i, row[j] equals membership of T[..i] in P[..j]. Fixing a row retains all text prefixes with the same vector of prefix memberships; in-place diagonal/above temporaries preserve the previous row observations until used.

Replacing any nonempty run of consecutive stars by one star preserves the recognized full-string language, since all nonnegative compositions of consumed lengths have the same possible total. This law does not replace or remove question marks.

If P has q nonstar tokens, every accepted text has length at least q; with no stars length must equal q. A pattern of q question marks accepts exactly length q. All stars accept every finite text, including empty.
For a pattern containing neither '?' nor '*', L(P) is the singleton {P}. On this restricted pattern domain, a successful match fixes the input bytes; adding a wildcard generally restores ambiguity.

Under byte semantics a two-byte UTF-8 character needs two question marks; a scalar-aware counterfactual would require one. Backslash is literal even immediately before '*', so backslash-star accepts a literal backslash followed by any bytes, not a lone literal star.

For star at pattern position j, accepting (i,j+1) is equivalent to accepting (i,j) with zero new bytes OR (i-1,j+1) with one more byte, for i>0. Replacing OR by AND loses witnesses such as nonempty text matched by one star.

forward:
Define P(text) by trimming lines, dropping empty lines and lines beginning '#', removing repeated '- ' prefixes, then concatenating babi::split_sentences outputs in line order. For tell let P=[s1,...,sk], S0=S and D contain actual returned read(Si-1,si)=(Si,ri). Fold Ok(None) into a success count; append (si,reason) for Ok(Some(reason)) or Err(error), with errors converted by Display. T(S,text,D)=(Sk,ok,gaps); no rollback is added.

For reply let q=trim(line). If q ends in '?', ask(S,q): Ok((a,w)) with a!='?' renders `a. Because: w`; sentinel a='?' renders `I do not know: w`; error renders `I do not know: e`. Otherwise T supplies the outcome: no gaps renders `Understood (k sentence[s]).`, singular exactly when k=1; gaps render `I do not understand: ` followed by ordered `«sentence» — reason` entries joined with `; `. Tags and D are model witnesses, not runtime String fields.

Nonempty Story paths are conditional source inspection. Native checks execute P and empty-projection tell/reply with seeded identity and state-lines observations.

forward:
S(F) prefixes `a {subj} ` and applies link/polarity templates: IsA -> `is a`/`is not a`; Has -> `has`/`does not have`; Can -> `can`/`cannot`; Does -> `does this:`/`does not do this:`. Other links use optional `not ` followed by know::link_name(link). Append space+obj, uppercase the body's first character, and append '.'.

key(F)=subj+'|'+Debug(link)+'|'+obj+'|'+negation. E(K,C) retains encounter-order Facts whose source starts `derived from` and whose key is absent from C. Q(K,C,n)=take_n(first-per-key(stable-sort-by-key(E))). Equal keys retain the first encounter's full Fact. The cache wrapper obtains C from checked(), an unexecuted filesystem boundary.

For list count L and request n, stride=max(1,floor(L/n)) when n>0, otherwise 1. I(L,n) takes the first n multiples of stride below L; I(L,0)=[]. round/write_world consume selected batches and cached verdicts; teacher T is a judgment, not a truth predicate.

forward: Delegate resource/endpoint validation and matching to Hopcroft-Karp. Let Z start at unmatched left vertices and close under unmatched L-to-R edges and matched R-to-L edges. Return sorted (L minus ZL, ZR). König equality makes the cover cardinality equal to maximum matching cardinality.
inverse: Universe: valid graph/count inputs crossed with candidate sorted vertex subsets, together with typed validation errors. Absent behaviors include any uncovered edge, size unequal to maximum matching size, an out-of-range/duplicate/unsorted member, or selecting ZL on the left instead of its complement. With fixed deterministic matching and closure Z, every pair except (L minus ZL,ZR) is absent. Invalid inputs cannot return a cover; resource errors precede endpoint errors. This is an exact source-derived specification with partial finite correspondence, not a proof.

For fixed cover (A,B), compatible antecedents are all bounded valid graphs whose deterministic alternating closure has ZL=L minus A and ZR=B; equivalently retain the matching/closure existential intermediate constrained by the actual deterministic Hopcroft-Karp traversal. Merely requiring A,B to cover edges is insufficient. Edge duplicates and extra isolated right vertices can have the same cover, so recovery is ambiguous. Empty graphs with zero or one right vertex both yield empty cover. Error fibers retain all graphs with the same first failing validation field.
limitations: Finite evidence, not proof; allocation failure unmodeled.

nodes.description: Original stable_marriage mod.rs and bounded models
forward: Validate equal sizes, checked quadratic budget, then proposer and receiver rows. Build receiver inverse ranks. FIFO free proposers propose to the next untried receiver; a receiver retains its best proposal so far and requeues the rejected proposer. Return receiver index per proposer when the queue empties.
inverse: Universe: two preference matrices crossed with candidate receiver vectors and errors. Absent successful behaviors include a non-permutation, a blocking pair (p,r) where both prefer each other to assigned mates, or a stable permutation giving a proposer a worse partner than another stable permutation. Invalid row lengths/permutations cannot succeed. Unequal sizes beat the budget error, which beats malformed rows; within each row, length beats duplicate/out-of-range entry. The finite exhaustive oracle supports these exact source-derived constraints without a general Rust proof.

For an observed permutation m, retain every pair of complete preference matrices for which m is stable and proposer-optimal: for each stable alternative s and proposer p, rank_p(m[p]) <= rank_p(s[p]). This finite relational characterization is ambiguous: with two proposers each ranking a distinct receiver first, either strict ordering in each receiver row still yields m. Observing a matching loses unproposed suffixes and proposal/rejection history. Error preimages comprise all profiles sharing the first failed validation predicate and observed indices.
limitations: Finite evidence, not proof; allocation failure unmodeled.
Partial syntax, no macro expansion or semantic AST.

nodes.description: Reject n<2; handle even n; write n-1=d*2^s for odd n. For each fixed reduced base a!=0, require a^d=1 or a^(d*2^j)=-1 for some 0<=j<s. Return true iff every witness passes. The full-u64 seven-witness theorem is an external finite-range premise, attributed to Jim Sinclair by the deterministic variants table at https://miller-rabin.appspot.com/. Rabin (1980) supplies the strong probable-prime background, not this witness-set provenance.

nodes.description: Validate p>=2, then deterministic is_prime(p), before reducing a. p=2 or residue zero returns a%p. Euler criterion rejects nonresidues. For p-1=q*2^s, find the first quadratic nonresidue z by ascending search, set c=z^q, x=a^((q+1)/2), t=a^q, m=s. While t!=1, choose least i with t^(2^i)=1; multiply x by c^(2^(m-i-1)), square that correction into c, update t and m=i. Return min(x,p-x). Tonelli-Shanks follows the method described by Shanks, Five Number-Theoretic Algorithms (1972).

While t!=1, choose least i with t^(2^i)=1; multiply x by c^(2^(m-i-1)), square that correction into c, update t and m=i. Return min(x,p-x). nodes.description: floor_sum mod.rs exact std-only bounded implementation and checks
forward: Reject m=0 first. Repeatedly add n(n-1)/2 * floor(a/m) and n*floor(b/m), checking each nonnegative contribution and sum. Reduce a,b modulo m. If a*n+b<m return accumulator; otherwise replace n by floor((a*n+b)/m), b by its remainder, and swap a,m.
inverse: Excluded pairs are Ok with any value different from the exact sum, ZeroModulus with m>0, Overflow for a representable sum, and success for m=0 or an unrepresentable sum.

For output Ok(s), compatible inputs are exactly positive-modulus tuples with sum s within u128. They are highly nonunique: (3,2,1,0) and (1,7,99,7) both give 1. ZeroModulus reconstructs m=0 but no other parameter; Overflow reconstructs positive m with sum above u128::MAX.
For representable parameter shifts a'=a+k*m,b'=b+l*m with nonnegative k,l, the sum increases by k*n(n-1)/2+l*n. Machine comparisons require both results representable.
For n<u64::MAX and representable sums, S(n+1)-S(n)=floor((a*n+b)/m). This provides an independent local boundary observation.
After stripping quotients, let h=a*n+b and h>=m. Remaining lattice count is S(floor(h/m),a,m,h mod m). When h<m the remaining count is zero. The swapped denominator is positive.

For n=0 and m>0 the sum is zero; m=0 still errors first. With a=0 the answer is n*floor(b/m) and fits u128. With m=1 and full-width n,a, the sum can exceed u128. Dividing an even triangle factor before multiplication avoids an unnecessary intermediate overflow.

nodes.description: two_way_matching exact byte algorithm
forward: Return the ascending set {i | text[i..i+m]=pattern}; for m=0 return all n+1 byte boundaries. Critical factorization plus periodic memory implements Crochemore-Perrin (JACM 38, 1991).

Both ordered maximal suffix scans choose a critical cut. Right-half mismatch advances past impossible starts; after a complete right match, the left half certifies the candidate. A periodic shift retains only the prefix guaranteed by the pattern period.
inverse: No false or omitted offsets are allowed. Matching does not decode Unicode, fold case, or remove overlapping occurrences.

For fixed pattern and offsets, the fiber consists of texts with exactly those occurrences and no others. Empty offsets generally admit many texts; even one match does not recover bytes outside the matched intervals.
A cut and period retain patterns whose maximal suffix in one of two opposing byte orders attains that cut with the recorded period. They do not uniquely recover a pattern.
If the critical prefix equals the prefix displaced by period, a successful right-half scan permits retaining m-period bytes after shifting. Memory is cleared on a right-half mismatch.
Empty pattern has n+1 matches, including the end boundary. A longer nonempty pattern has no matches; these cases bypass factorization.
Any bijection of byte values preserves occurrence offsets although it may change the critical factorization and intermediate shifts.

nodes.description: needleman_wunsch exact byte algorithm
forward: Maximize the sum of match/mismatch/gap signed i64 scores over all global monotone paths. Store one deterministic optimum, preferring diagonal then deletion then insertion at every traceback cell. Origin: Needleman-Wunsch, JMB 48 (1970).

Cell (i,j) is the best representable prefix score; all three candidate additions are checked before selection. Traceback steps consume one or both input bytes and never produce gap-gap. Every path terminates at (0,0).
inverse: Successful results cannot omit input bytes, contain gap-gap columns, or have a suboptimal score. This is global linear-gap byte alignment; there are no affine gaps, local alignment or sequence-specific assumptions.

Deleting None entries independently from each column side uniquely reconstructs the two inputs. A score alone admits many input pairs; even complete columns do not recover scoring parameters uniquely.

Checked dimensions precede CellLimit and allocations. Boundary scores are checked before interior cells. ScoreOverflow may reject even when the mathematically best path fits, because every candidate addition is checked.

Strict greater-than replacement preserves diagonal on a tie; deletion wins a deletion/insertion tie when diagonal is worse. This local traceback rule selects one optimal path, not a lexicographically minimum forward alignment.
A table cell retains every optimal path to its two prefixes, but only one predecessor is recorded. Discarded optimal alternatives cannot be recovered from that predecessor alone.
Multiplying all scores by a positive integer preserves the chosen path when every intermediate checked sum remains representable. Overflow changes the admissible domain, so this is a conditional law.

Outside the L1 ball, its projection equals signed simplex projection of magnitudes and soft threshold at the common active magnitude difference. nodes.cost: Cholesky O(n³), triangular O(n²), QR O(m*n²), stationary O(k*n²); O(m*n+n²) inputs/work; n<=64,m<=128,iterations<=10000.
nodes.description: Factor bounded symmetric systems, solve triangular systems, minimize linear least squares and iterate linear solves with fresh residuals.
forward: Factor bounded symmetric systems, solve triangular systems, minimize linear least squares and iterate linear solves with fresh residuals.
Cholesky A=L*Lᵀ transports b through lower and upper solves. QR normal equations transport least squares to a quadratic. Stationary solvers share Ax=b but not trajectories.
inverse: At the real-model level, exclude nontriangular Cholesky factors or A!=L*Lᵀ, triangular solutions with T*x!=b, and least-squares candidates with Aᵀ(A*x-b)!=0. These exact exclusions describe targets, not an exact-equality acceptance test for f64 outputs. The native relation excludes reports differing from rounded factor/solve transitions, incorrect recomputed reconstruction/primal/normal residuals, or a stationary Converged status when its computed residual exceeds tolerance. A small native residual does not exclude large coordinate error on ill-conditioned inputs; numerical rank is not certified by unpivoted QR.

For fixed real triangular T and observed x, compatible right sides satisfy b=T*x; allowing T to vary gives many systems with the same solution. For fixed full-column-rank A, the real QR least-squares fiber for x is b=A*x+z with Aᵀz=0, so nonzero orthogonal residuals remain compatible. A real positive-diagonal Cholesky factor uniquely determines A=L*Lᵀ, while rounded native factor/report fibers can include neighboring matrices. Stationary output plus residual/status leaves many initial vectors, budgets and systems compatible; native antecedents must reproduce the rounded execution, not merely these real identities.
limitations: Positive pivots in floating arithmetic do not certify spectral conditioning. Unpivoted QR rejects exact zero encountered pivots only. Stationary convergence requires matrix properties not inferred from finite success.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
nodes.state: Dimensions and coordinates agree; residual, reconstruction residual and normal residual are different observations; explicit errors/statuses retained.

nodes.cost: Scalar O(k) callbacks; dense quadratic O(k*n²), Lasso O(k*m*n) plus objective/residual checks; leaf dimensions and iteration caps apply.
nodes.description: Bounded scalar minimization and sufficient-decrease search, box/simplex quadratic optimization, and coordinate Lasso descent.
forward: Bounded scalar minimization and sufficient-decrease search, box/simplex quadratic optimization, and coordinate Lasso descent.

Directional quadratic restrictions connect Armijo to Brent; QR normal equations connect least squares to constrained optimization on fixtures with feasible minimizer; orthogonal Lasso reduces to soft threshold.
inverse: For real convex quadratic minimization on C, exclude infeasible x or b-Q*x outside N_C(x); for Lasso exclude Aᵀ(A*x-y)+lambda*s!=0 for every s in the L1 subgradient. For a supplied scalar restriction, exclude an Armijo step violating its sufficient-decrease inequality and a claimed global Brent minimizer outside the stipulated unimodal target. Native finite reports instead obey rounded transition/stopping relations: box projected-step residual, simplex FW gap and Lasso KKT residual are distinct. Exclude switching the minus-linear convention, using objective error as coordinate error, exceeding callback budget or relabeling exhausted/stagnated reports. Native Converged does not assert the exact real KKT equalities.

For fixed real Q,C and feasible optimizer x, compatible linear terms lie in Q*x+N_C(x); thus a boundary optimizer generally does not identify b. Identity-design Lasso with lambda fixed gives y_i=x_i+lambda*sign(x_i) for nonzero x_i, while x_i=0 admits every y_i in [-lambda,lambda]. General designs admit y with Aᵀ(y-A*x) in lambda*partial||x||1, including null(Aᵀ) perturbations. Brent and Armijo observations retain many callbacks agreeing at the sampled points but differing elsewhere; a step does not recover its direction or original objective. These are real target fibers; matching a native report additionally requires matching its rounded path, validation and status.
limitations: Scalar unimodality/differentiability are caller premises. Projected step residual and FW floating gap are not unconditional distance/certified objective bounds. Tightened PSD admission rejects some valid PSD matrices.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
nodes.state: Quadratic objective is .5*xQx-linear*x; Lasso is .5||Ax-y||²+lambda||x||1. Scalar bracket, feasible set, stationarity measure and termination status remain tagged.

nodes.cost: Barycentric O(n²) evaluation, monotone cubic O(n), de Casteljau O(n²); Gauss<=5 callbacks; Romberg<=20 levels and explicit evaluation budget. Finite allocation/stack limits retained.
nodes.description: Evaluate interpolation polynomials and shape-preserving cubics, Bernstein curves and bounded quadrature.
forward: Evaluate interpolation polynomials and shape-preserving cubics, Bernstein curves and bounded quadrature.

A fixed polynomial can be represented by Lagrange nodes and Bernstein controls; quadrature integrates resulting callback. Affine monotone cubic equals the line, providing an independent exact real integral.
inverse: For the real target, exclude a Lagrange polynomial failing its nodal equations, a Bernstein evaluation outside the control convex hull for t in[0,1], and shape-preserving cubic segments with overshoot contrary to their slope construction. Conditional Gauss polynomial exactness excludes wrong integrals only for the stated degree premise in real arithmetic. Native f64 results are not required to satisfy those identities bit-for-bit: their complement contains wrong rounded recurrences, wrong basis/interval coordinates, incorrect knot return values, excess callbacks or inaccurate status bookkeeping. Romberg estimated_error=0 does not exclude a nonzero true integral error; unknown off-sample function behavior remains allowed.

At fixed distinct nodes and fixed degree<n, a complete set of real nodal ordinates identifies the interpolation polynomial, but one evaluated ordinate leaves an affine coefficient fiber. At Bernstein t=0 only the first control is observed and all later controls remain free; at interior t, perturbations of controls whose Bernstein-weighted sum is zero retain the value. Monotone sample data do not identify the true between-node function. For quadrature samples x_j, f and f+h with h(x_j)=0 have the same sampled execution but may have different integrals; h can be a scaled squared product of (x-x_j). Native rounded equality may enlarge these fibers, and callback budget/status do not restore unsampled information.
limitations: Polynomial/basis identities are real arithmetic. Shape preservation does not bound error against unknown original function. Romberg diagonal differences can miss unsampled structure and are heuristic.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
nodes.state: Node domain/spacing and basis coordinates remain explicit; no extrapolation for interpolators; quadrature errors and statuses remain distinct from true-integral certificates.

nodes.description: Exact integer subset/knapsack objectives and structured matrix/partition/tree dynamic programming with explicit work and allocation bounds.
forward: Exact integer subset/knapsack objectives and structured matrix/partition/tree dynamic programming with explicit work and allocation bounds.

Weight=profit subset embedding links target reachability with attainable knapsack objectives. Totally-monotone identity minima transport coordinates into convex interval costs and positive BST weights in the harness.
inverse: For exact integer targets, exclude a bitset true decision with no subset summing to target, a knapsack objective unattainable under capacity or below the feasible maximum, a SMAWK column that is not the leftmost row minimum, a partition value violating the minimum over exactly the requested nonempty contiguous intervals, or a BST value violating the successful-key interval recurrence. SMAWK/partition exclusions are conditional on total-monotonicity/monotone-split premises: arbitrary callbacks outside those premises may yield incorrect answers without validation errors. Native categorical exclusions also include overflow wraparound, violating word/state/cell or callback caps, and returning partial answers on budget failure. These integer targets do not carry f64 tolerances.

A reachability true output retains all item multisets having at least one target-sum subset; false retains those having none. For [1,1] at target1, two distinct index masks share the same decision and knapsack objective, and objective-only output does not recover either witness. Fixed SMAWK minima j_i constrain each lawful row by M[i,j_i]<=M[i,j] and strict inequality for earlier j on ties; row offsets preserve minimizer indices while changing values. A partition scalar retains many interval-cost arrays and boundary choices, subject to nonempty contiguous ranges and structural premises; it does not reconstruct a split witness. BST cost similarly admits different weight vectors or tied optimal trees. Checked integer values are exact when successful under the stated premises, while an error identifies only a broad resource/domain fiber.
limitations: SMAWK every submatrix must have monotone leftmost minima; merely full-matrix monotone minima is insufficient. Partition monotone optima must hold at every layer. These properties are not verified dynamically. BST is successful-key-only objective.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
nodes.state: Exact feasible objectives, caller structural assumptions, checked integer arithmetic and leftmost ties retain distinct contracts. Resource errors never masquerade as approximation.

forward: boot: adopt (pid, starttime, argv suffix) or autostart unless stopped; tick: reap, restart after 5..300 s doubling backoff, escalate marker -> SIGTERM -> SIGKILL, run nvidia-smi/probe gate before any gpu spawn.

nodes.description: Config-declared work-flow probes of continuously running workers: input queue, backlog and quarantine stacks, progress and limit markers, latched with hysteresis into starved/clogged/stalled/limited plus a quarantine-rate anomaly, and one bounded decision per transition.
nodes.state: run_root/flow/state.json (latches, last progress, samples, quarantine-rate windows and latches, Crab-made pause flag, hold) and append-only run_root/flow/journal.jsonl.
forward: read(source) counts dir entries, JSONL lines, a JSON integer or equality, mtime or a sum; unknown is an error, never zero. assess: starved = input < low_water; clogged = stack > high_water until <= resume_at; stalled = input >= 1 and progress unchanged >= stall_seconds; limited = fresh tail matches a pattern; latch after hysteresis evaluations; decision precedence limited > clogged > starved > stalled; apply starts a stopped not-explicitly-stopped producer, creates/removes only Crab's own pause file, restarts once per stall by policy, or reports.

Stacks have a role: a backlog may pause its producer (clogged = backlog > high_water until <= resume_at); a quarantine (cumulative quarantined and finished counts) never pauses: the anomaly dquarantined/dfinished > max_rate over rate_window_seconds with >= min_finished finished is reported once per rise with an optional dominant reason. A pausing backlog named like a quarantine is refused at load. Load migration clears a Crab-paused clog whose recorded over-high-water stacks no longer pause, so the first evaluation removes Crab's own pause file. stable_facts feeds the council fingerprint.
inverse: Excluded: killing in-flight work, starting an explicitly stopped producer, removing a foreign pause file, restarting without policy or during a limit hold, acting on unknown readings.
The journal recovers which values led to each transition and action; raw files between evaluations are not reconstructed.
Excluded: pausing on a quarantine stack; removing a pause file that is not exactly Crab's; migrating a clog whose over-list is unknown or still includes a pausing backlog.
nodes.cost: Per evaluation and probe: bounded reads (<= 100000 dir entries, JSON <= 1 MiB, JSONL <= 256 MiB, tails <= 1 MiB, 4 newest entries per glob segment); measured 2026-11-04: ten live Fish/Eel probes in about 30 ms; one journal line per transition.

nodes.description: Event-driven council of named consultant Dolphins over Crab's supervision digest (rounds on fact changes or after the longest interval, quorum of idle members, member timeout), typed verdict parsing, deterministic combination and the Octopus's attention queue with fingerprint merging.
nodes.state: run_root/council/{state.json, journal.jsonl, refusals.jsonl}; run_root/attention/{attention.jsonl, state.json, attention.md}.
forward: tick: a compact skip unless the stable-facts fingerprint changed and min_spacing passed, or period passed; below quorum idle members a skip; else the same bounded digest is queued to each idle member (busy ones absent); close when all asked answered or after member_timeout (silent ones timed out): parse first line VERDICT none|octopus|action:<allowed>:<probe>|capacity:<kind>:<more|fewer>:<n>; combine over the answers (fewer than quorum -> expired attention item): all none -> journal, identical allowed action -> execute through flow bounds, otherwise attention item. Attention items are fingerprinted by source and facts; repeats merge (count, first/last time) and only new fingerprints are appended.
inverse: Excluded: executing a capacity verdict, a one-sided or disagreeing action, any malformed or unknown verdict, any text beyond the typed first line.
The journal recovers each round's verdicts, reasons (bounded) and answer hashes; the answers' full texts stay in the consult reports.
Excluded: a round on unchanged facts before the longest interval; overwriting a busy member's task; combining fewer than quorum (>= 2) answers; appending a repeat of a known attention fingerprint.
nodes.cost: At most one consult-queue entry per member per min_spacing (>= 60 s), one per period (>= 600 s) on unchanged facts; one digest composition and fingerprint per check_seconds; a digest <= max_task_bytes; attention state <= 512 fingerprints.

nodes.description: Holder of one Dolphin terminal as a Crab worker: host-wide singleton lock, create or adopt a tmux session running the configured command, optional pin of a self-updating CLI, graceful SIGTERM stop, exit when the session or command ends; never sends keys.
nodes.state: Exclusive flock held for the holder's lifetime (owner record pid/session/socket), the held command's (pid, starttime), pin recheck clock.
forward: lock busy -> AlreadyRunning(5); pin fails -> Unpinned(6); session exists: one live pane whose pane process or direct child runs the command (basename of argv0, equal arguments, #! interpreter prefix allowed) -> adopted, else Conflict(3) untouched; else new-session -d with command plus rendered prompt argument, owner option. Poll: stop flag -> SIGTERM command, wait grace 1..8 s, kill-session; session gone or command gone -> Ended(0); pin recheck every 60 s, failure -> stop and Unpinned.
inverse: Excluded: a second holder of one lock, keystrokes (send-keys/load-buffer/paste-buffer), touching a conflicting session, starting an unpinned program, an unbound or unused prompt placeholder.
From an exit status one recovers the outcome class only; the owner record names the last holder, not earlier ones.
nodes.cost: Per poll: has-session (one tmux client) and one /proc stat read; adoption scans /proc once for direct children (bounded 65536 entries); the pin hashes one file and runs one bounded version command (15 s) per check.

read_with(markdown, cap): every admitted sentence also gets whole clauses (clause.rs, verbatim cap) and its noun lemmas; a table or figure caption is restated as «Table N shows …»; a sentence whose whole parse yields no clause is tried by its comma/semicolon segments; splits after «et al.», «e.g.», «i.e.», «cf.», «Fig.», «Eq.», «Sec.», «vs.», «etc.» are joined; a standalone title-case line between prose paragraphs opens a part (PDF subsection titles); acronym definitions «Long Form (ACR)» are collected as the paper's own knowledge. nodes.description: Whole clauses from Mova's UD tree of a paper sentence, restated in the describer's perspective: clause splitting (conj, parataxis, subject relative clauses), shared subjects and auxiliaries, we/our -> the authors/their, bracketed spans left out, past passives with a by-agent turned active, and a verbatim cap enforced by moving adverbial clauses and obliques (fronted or put last) before leaving out optional modifiers.
forward: clauses(tree, toks, cap): heads = root + conj (of a clause head, fixed point) + parataxis with subject + acl:relcl with a relative-pronoun subject and a nominal antecedent; per head: subtree minus other heads, brackets removed; conj without subject takes the governor's subject (and its auxiliaries for VBN/VBG); relcl replaces the pronoun with the antecedent phrase; main clause with its own non-'to' marker refused; activize (was/were + VBN == past form + by-agent); loop: build (perspective, own cc removed, edge trimming, doubled punctuation, lowered opener) -> verbatim run in alphanumeric source tokens; if > cap choose the step with key (reaches cap?, move before drop, removed size, rank advmod<advcl<obl<appos<acl<amod<nmod, index), at most 8 steps; accept 4..60 words, finite verb (or activized), head kept, subject kept, no wh/cc/own-marker opener, letters >= 70%, balanced quotes.

2026-11-04 additions: «Note that X» -> X; a coordinated VB under a VBP governor without auxiliaries counts as finite; a subordinate root with a realized coordinated/paratactic clause under it is attached after that clause (fragment(): mark kept, cap, 3..30 words); an uncovered oblique/adverbial clause/adverb phrase of a realized head restated with the head's core (split()); an uncovered apposition or VBN participle of a covered noun restated as «N is/are M» (predication()); a moved fronted block goes before the closing punctuation; question(): «The paper asks: …?».
noted(): the complement of a sentence-initial «Note that …» is the dependent of «note» opened by «that» that is ccomp or a predicate with its own subject, whatever its relation label (2026-11-05).
inverse: Not done: paraphrase beyond these operations, present or modal passives, object relative clauses, verb agreement repair, pronoun resolution beyond the authors' we, meaning checks of a dropped modifier (a dropped obligatory oblique can leave 'relies solely'), repairing Mova's wrong roots (long sentences parsed with a noun root yield nothing and become teaching material). Counterexample 2026-11-04: «For instance, the participant role doesn't make a difference would be labeled as ARG0 …» after a misparse.

Dropped content is not recoverable from the clause alone; no unique inverse is claimed.
A «that»-marked dependent without a subject or predicate under a non-ccomp label is not taken as the noted clause.

nodes.description: The `layer` source: improve an existing dictionary layer in place through review-only proposals. Reads the layer file (records, judaism-senses, emode-senses or mystic-senses), finds weak rows natively, asks the teacher only for weak rows with evidence, `batch` asked rows per question with the pupils' numbered senses and only the weak fields, and turns the answer into proposal lines in the builder's own format. Source: `tools/nautilus/src/improve.rs`.
nodes.state: Parent: `nautilus`. Implements work::Job for the loop and the pool; animal::Config::job builds it; pool.rs counts its open items.
forward: parse: line -> its exact tab columns (render = join, byte-identical). weakness(format,row,base): records meaning<40 or sense<80 or examples<3; judaism no primary record and no own pos/meaning, or >=2 examples and neither sense nor interpretation; emode an empty modern/meaning/difference; mystic sense<80 or no primary record and no meaning. askable = weak and (an example, or a sense for records/mystic). LayerJob.next(seen) = the first ten askable rows of part `part` (FNV(word) mod parts) whose words are in no seen key `<layer>:w1+w2...`. validate: lines with exactly the format's fields, each `-` or 2..1200 chars without date or control characters; >= half of the asked words well formed, else rejected; proposal = the changed lines, rebuilt in the target columns (examples, kind, forms, tests and note from the row; pos/meaning empty when the base has the word, as the builder writes); none changed: rejected as kept.

2026-11-04 (senses): askable also needs a non-junk word and min_uses examples using it (lemmas; judaism/emode 2); asked_fields = the weak fields only; plan_row: native pick when every asked field is sense-like; answer = word, pick, asked fields; absent lines rejected; a restated sense field dropped and marked `restates sense N`; `# pick` lines; items of `batch` asked rows (native rows ride along).
inverse: Behavior complement: Never writes the layer file or the builder's senses files; never asks a thin row (fewer than two corpus examples) or a row without evidence; never writes examples for corpus-quoted formats; never admits. Evidence status: source-derived model with finite checks, not a proof.

Reverse reconstruction: A proposal line and the row it came from recover which fields the teacher changed (the others are the row's); the item key recovers the asked words. No unique inverse is claimed: an all-`-` answer and no answer both leave the row as it is.
nodes.cost: One read and parse of the layer file per next/open call (20 MB primary layer: about 0.1 s); one question of at most 12000 bytes per ten rows.

forward: step(now): current(assignment) = the lease if it names a job and now < expires_unix (another member's lease is an error; a released or missing file is none) -> none: report idle; layer = params.layer; unconfigured: report refused; a draft layer not made: animal::make natively, report working; else Config::job(layer, part, parts) and work::Loop{ledger = LEDGERS/<layer>/ledger.jsonl, member} .step -> backlog(layer) writes LEDGERS/<layer>/backlog.json (open items of the whole job) -> report state = finished (loop idle) | stopped (limit) | working. run: steps every SECS (x4 when idle/waiting/stopped/refused) until STOP.

nodes.description: Work pools in Crab's flow configuration: members (a configured worker, an assignment file Crab writes, a report file the member writes) and jobs (priority, backlog probe, parts, licence line, opaque params). Crab leases one unit (job, part) to each idle member and journals every assignment and release. No member-specific code. Source: `tools/crab/src/pool.rs`.
nodes.state: Parent: `crab-orchestration`. Flow owns the pools (FlowConfig.pools, Flow.tick, status, kinds, capacity), so flow_status, the council digest and the capacity review show them; releases for stopped or refused members become attention items through the flow events. The member side is mova-nautilus-pool.
forward: tick(t): read every job's backlog (flow::read; unknown is None) and member report (<= 64 KiB). For each lease: job gone -> release; report for this lease says finished/refused -> done[unit] = backlog, release; stopped -> release; t >= expires -> release (expired); worker running and (report fresh: unix + lease > t, or t < assigned + lease) -> expires = t + lease, rewrite. done[unit] is dropped once its job's backlog reading changes. Waiting units: backlog > 0 known, not held, not done; sorted by priority desc, backlog desc, job, part. Idle members (worker running, no lease, report not stopped) in name order take them pairwise; lease id = pool-seq. check(): no unit held twice. status: English lines (`m works on job; the lease runs n s more.`, `m is idle.`, `job waits with a backlog of n.`) and a view; capacity: backlog totals per pool.
inverse: Behavior complement: Never starts, stops or signals a worker; never assigns to a member whose worker is not running or whose report says stopped; never splits a job that does not declare parts; never interprets params; never enforces a job's licence (the member does). Evidence status: source-derived model with finite checks, not a proof.

Reverse reconstruction: pools.jsonl recovers every lease (member, job, part, id, expiry, backlog at assignment) and every release with its reason; pools.json the current leases and done units. Readings between ticks are not reconstructed.
nodes.cost: Per tick and pool: one bounded read per job backlog and per member report, at most one atomic write per member; members <= 32, jobs <= 64, parts <= 16.
