nodes.description: Wikitext of one definition, example or list line → plain text plus side records (labels, form-of lemma, nyms, examples, gaps, dropped). Template calls are found with brace nesting, split at top-level pipes (not inside nested templates or links) into positional and named parameters; each known name has a handler printing what the template prints (links → alt or term, w → display or article, taxlink → name, gloss/qualifier → bracketed text, form-of → «Kind lemma», place → «A kind in holonyms», ux → example recorded); category, sense-id and maintenance templates print nothing and are counted as dropped; any other name prints nothing and is counted as a gap. Links [[a|b]] → b, external [url text] → text, bold/italic quotes, comments, references and HTML tags removed, entities decoded, whitespace collapsed.
forward: Wikitext of one definition, example or list line → plain text plus side records (labels, form-of lemma, nyms, examples, gaps, dropped). Template calls are found with brace nesting, split at top-level pipes (not inside nested templates or links) into positional and named parameters; each known name has a handler printing what the template prints (links → alt or term, w → display or article, taxlink → name, gloss/qualifier → bracketed text, form-of → «Kind lemma», place → «A kind in holonyms», ux → example recorded); category, sense-id and maintenance templates print nothing and are counted as dropped; any other name prints nothing and is counted as a gap. Links [[a|b]] → b, external [url text] → text, bold/italic quotes, comments, references and HTML tags removed, entities decoded, whitespace collapsed.
inverse: Never executes Lua modules or expands templates from the dump's Template namespace: unknown templates contribute no text (only a gap count), categories are not reproduced, inline modifiers other than the first term segment are dropped, nested templates inside dropped templates are not visited, unclosed {{ or [[ are left as literal text.

Many wikitexts render to the same text (any template with no handler, any drop-listed template, bold vs plain, [[a|b]] vs b); from a rendered text and its side records one can recover the set of compatible lines only up to these erasures: labels and nyms are recoverable as values, not as template names or positions.
limitations: Well-formed UTF-8 wikitext/XML of the English Wiktionary dump export format; Lua modules not executed; partial syntax and bounded synthetic checks plus one corpus-scale observation (2026-11-04); no universal proof or percentage surrogate.
nodes.state: render is pure and deterministic (BTreeMap counts); output has no tab or newline; a template either prints text, is dropped (counted) or is a gap (counted), never silently removed.
nodes.cost: O(n) passes over a line of n bytes per nesting level (close_braces rescans nested bodies; parameters rendered recursively): worst case O(n·d) for depth d; tidy is O(n) with a few replace passes. Memory O(n).

nodes.description: A page's wikitext → its ==English== section (to the next level-2 heading or ----) → entries: each part-of-speech heading (fixed list) under the current etymology number is one entry; its first template line is the head (forms from en-noun/en-verb/en-adj/en-adv/en-proper noun/head parameters, head labels from tlb); # and ## lines are senses rendered by wikitext::render; #: lines add examples and in-sense nyms to the last sense; #* lines count quotations; Synonyms/Antonyms subsections add section nyms from l/col/syn templates and plain links. Logical lines join lines while templates are open. Entries without senses are dropped. row() formats 13 tab-separated cells: word, pos, numbered meaning with bracketed labels, empty lesson sense, numbered examples, etymology note, labels, synonyms, antonyms, forms, form-of, gaps, provenance.
forward: A page's wikitext → its ==English== section (to the next level-2 heading or ----) → entries: each part-of-speech heading (fixed list) under the current etymology number is one entry; its first template line is the head (forms from en-noun/en-verb/en-adj/en-adv/en-proper noun/head parameters, head labels from tlb); # and ## lines are senses rendered by wikitext::render; #: lines add examples and in-sense nyms to the last sense; #* lines count quotations; Synonyms/Antonyms subsections add section nyms from l/col/syn templates and plain links. Logical lines join lines while templates are open. Entries without senses are dropped. row() formats 13 tab-separated cells: word, pos, numbered meaning with bracketed labels, empty lesson sense, numbered examples, etymology note, labels, synonyms, antonyms, forms, form-of, gaps, provenance.
inverse: Does not read other language sections, translation subpages, Thesaurus pages, pronunciation, etymology text, quotation text, Usage notes, Derived/Related terms, Alternative forms or Translations; forms are not computed by the Lua module (irregular forms only when written as parameters; inline specifications kept raw); a POS heading outside the fixed list is not an entry.

From a row one recovers the page title, part of speech, sense texts and counts, labels and nyms per sense, the head forms and the exact source location (page id, revision, file, stream offset) — so the original wikitext is recoverable from the dump, not from the row; the row itself is a lossy projection (template names, quotation texts and dropped sections are not recoverable).
limitations: Well-formed UTF-8 wikitext/XML of the English Wiktionary dump export format; Lua modules not executed; partial syntax and bounded synthetic checks plus one corpus-scale observation (2026-11-04); no universal proof or percentage surrogate.
nodes.state: Each row has exactly 13 cells, no tab or newline inside a cell; sense numbers are 1..k for top-level senses and k.j for subsenses; an entry has at least one sense; gaps of a row are the sum of its lines' gaps.
nodes.cost: O(L) per page section of L bytes plus render costs per line; memory O(L) for logical lines and the entries.

nodes.description: page: index lookup of the given titles, their streams decoded, rows printed. build: every part's index read (MultiBzDecoder) → distinct stream offsets; a job queue of (part, offset) consumed by N threads, each decoding one bz2 stream (BzDecoder stops at the stream end), parsing its pages (quick_xml, unmatched end tags allowed) and turning ns-0 pages with an English section into rows with provenance; the first error stops the queue (fail-fast); rows sorted by (lower-case title, not-lower-case flag, title, index in page) and written after a CC BY-SA header; gaps.tsv sorted by count; report.json (counts, seconds, peak RSS); module.json with each file's SHA-256 and size. check: re-hashes the listed files. cover: streams a layer and reports a word list's exact and case-folded coverage.

From the module one recovers the dump name and files and, per row, the stream that held its page (file + offset): decompressing that stream and re-running entry::entries reproduces the row; the layer bytes are independent of the thread count (sorted output), so they do not reveal it.
limitations: Well-formed UTF-8 wikitext/XML of the English Wiktionary dump export format; Lua modules not executed; partial syntax and bounded synthetic checks plus one corpus-scale observation (2026-11-04); no universal proof or percentage surrogate.
nodes.state: module.json lists exactly the files written with their current SHA-256 and byte size; the layer's first line declares CC BY-SA; rows are sorted by sort_key.
nodes.cost: Time ≈ (decompressed bytes / per-thread bz2 throughput) / threads + parse; measured on the English edition (2.01 GB bz2, 108 963 streams): 63–105 s wall at 6 threads, 100 s at 3 threads on a shared machine (2026-11-04). nodes.cost: hits O(n²) per sentence of n words (child scans and dominance walks); counting O(total words) plus one CoNLL-U parse per block of 5000 sentences; counts BTreeMap O(K log K) for K (lemma, source, path, class) keys; build O(K log K); feats O(log L) lookup in L lemmas; the table is loaded once per process (OnceLock).
nodes.description: A gender, number and animacy lexicon of common nouns counted from Mova's own parses over Bergsma and Lin's high-precision noun–pronoun paths, smoothed into per-lemma shares, and the mention features it gives the sieve and the frame reader.
forward: hits(s): for each third-person pronoun (he/him/his/himself, she/her/hers/herself, it/its/itself, they/them/their/themselves) and each acl:relcl on a noun, emit (noun lemma, class, path) for paths refl (reflexive under the subject's predicate, or emphatic directly under the noun without case), poss (nmod:poss in an obj/obl/iobj of the subject's predicate, outside the subject), say (subject of a SAY verb whose ccomp has the pronoun as nominative subject, same quote), pred (nominative pronoun subject of a copular noun without case, negation or clausal dependents), appos, relpron (first non-ADP word of the relative clause who/whom/whose or which). The noun must be countable (NOUN, not compound/flat/fixed/conj/goeswith/reparandum, no conj child, alphabetic lemma), in the pronoun's quote, without a what/which/whose determiner; a plural noun with a singular pronoun is dropped. feats(lemma): animacy ANIM if smoothed (masc+fem+who) share >= tau, INAN if the complement >= tau, with at least min_n counts; gender MASC, FEM, NEUT or MASC|FEM from smoothed he/she/it shares >= tau; contradictory (NEUT with ANIM, INAN with masc/fem) and empty results give None.
inverse: A table row is the sum over the corpus of path hits; it does not recover which sentences produced it beyond one example id per (lemma, source, path, class), and the shares do not recover counts. A Feats value is compatible with every row whose smoothed shares and evidence clear the same thresholds; None is compatible with missing lemmas, too little evidence, mixed shares and contradictory decisions alike.
limitations: Parser errors become counts (an adjective tagged NOUN after a copula, e.g. «content», gets person counts); the which/who columns include relative clauses attached to the wrong noun.
Measured only through GUM dev, the frame bench dev lines and school/Wikipedia train and cv courses (2026-11-04); no proof of precision; percentage surrogate unsupported.
nodes.state: One tree at a time for hits; Counts maps; a process-wide OnceLock table selected by COREF_GENDER, MOVA_DATA or HOME; COREF_GENDER_TAU, COREF_GENDER_MIN, COREF_GENDER_ALPHA, COREF_GENDER_INTERNAL environment snapshot.

nodes.cost: One open-addressing probe per lookup, O(1) expected at load factor <= 1/2, plus O(k) records; the acronym plural adds one probe. Blob compiled in (~20 MB); EN_LEXEXT read once.
nodes.description: The lexicon extension at run time: a second compiled blob of forms (tag, sources, lemma), lemma paradigms and acronym expansions, answering only for what the in-code dictionary lacks; the dictionary fingerprint and every trained model are untouched; EN_LEXEXT=0 turns it off.
forward: analyses(lower) = the form's records, or a synthetic NNPS for an -s plural of an acronym in capitals; known, tags, lemma(form, tag), form(lemma, tag), expansions(acronym, case-sensitive). hint(word, inside_cap) keeps acronym and two-capital records only for a word with two capitals, name-list-only and <= 3-letter proper records only for a capitalised word, and for a capitalised word inside a sentence only when a proper-noun record is left.
inverse: form(lemma, tag) recovers one form of the cell (several may share it); the written case is not recoverable from hint's tags.
Nothing is returned for: forms absent from the files (except acronym plurals), lower-case acronym keys, any lookup when EN_LEXEXT=0; hint is empty under the case gate.
limitations: Keys are lower case; case decisions live only in hint
No frequencies: records of one form are unordered
Acronyms read as NNP where EWT often writes NN with a lower-case lemma (ADHD, RFP)
nodes.state: Compiled lexext.bin and its layout constants; EN_LEXEXT OnceLock.

nodes.cost: One pass over SPECIALIST LRAGR (~121 MB) and LEXICON (~56 MB), the OEWN JSON entries and the name lists; BTreeMap rows; about 3 s on 2026-11-04.
nodes.description: Generator of the lexicon extension (en lexgrow): rows the dictionary lacks from Open English WordNet 2025, the SPECIALIST Lexicon 2026, 2010 U.S. Census surnames and the Names Corpus, with provenance per row, and acronyms with expansions; sorted, deterministic.
forward: SPECIALIST LRAGR single-token open-class rows mapped to PTB tags (NNP for a capitalised noun base; non-noun rows with two capitals dropped); units the dictionary covers in the class keep only an extra NNS of a dictionary NN lemma. OEWN lemmas: NNP for capitalised nouns, NN/VB/VBP/JJ/RB, listed irregular forms, regular morph forms only when SPECIALIST lacks the lemma and WordNet lists none (no plural for -s/-ism nouns). put skips dontuse forms, rows the dictionary has, and forms the dictionary has in the same class. Census (>= 1000 bearers) and Names Corpus names as NNP only when no source has them as common words. Common-word rows of <= 3 letters need a WordNet source. Acronyms: WordNet synset pairs by initials first, then SPECIALIST acronym_of, <= 8 each.
inverse: A row's source key (EUI, o, c, k; synset or EUI for acronyms) points back to its source record; dropped rows and other forms of covered units are not recoverable.

Never written: Wiktionary/Wikipedia material, multi-word entries, closed classes, variants of dictionary units (occured, noticable), dontuse forms, abbreviation adjectives, ungiven comparison (lexical), rare surnames, names that are common words.
limitations: SPECIALIST is biomedical-heavy; rare readings weigh like common ones in the hint
WordNet-only verbs with irregular forms get their base only
Mova's own trees are not a source (corpus 0.4 is CC BY-SA; trees drafted by an EWT-trained model)
nodes.state: Source files as read and the in-code dictionary; no network or randomness.

nodes.description: `mova fetch`: a release's files from the repository's manifest (releases/0.5-files.json, compiled in) over HTTPS, from the .torrent (info hash checked, BEP 19 web seed, every piece's SHA-1) or from the magnet link (xs source); size and SHA-256 must match before anything is unpacked; installs without deleting earlier files; the manifest's policy check and its Markdown page.
forward: check enforces URL/torrent/magnet derivation from base_url and trackers, hashes, safe paths, raw_bytes = sum of contents and the licence policy (model/corpus/dictionaries CC-BY-SA-4.0, modules not ours and optional, no Wikipedia/Wiktionary outside a module, only the model required); render_bone writes the page (usage via target/release/mova and the PATH line); `mova fetch --page` prints it.

fetch_one downloads by https, torrent or magnet into a .part, refuses a size or SHA-256 mismatch (removing the part), lists the tar.gz (members inside <top>), reuses a cached <unpack_to>/<top> only when its stamp names the archive and check_inventory passes (exactly the manifest contents: paths, sizes, SHA-256, no extra files or links), otherwise unpacks into staging that must pass the same check, verifies a module, and copies install entries, renaming a differing earlier target or a failed cache .before-<release>.
inverse: Behavior complement: no peer wire protocol, trackers, DHT or BEP 9; no multi-file or v2 torrents; no resume; no deletion of earlier installs; licences checked only against fixed policy rules.

Reverse reconstruction: earlier installs and failed caches survive as .before-<release>; the stamp gives the archive SHA-256 and hence the manifest row (the inventory check, not the stamp, vouches for the cached bytes); the way of fetching is not recorded.
limitations: Partial source model; finite tests with file:// fixtures (including tampered-cache negative controls) and one live run on 2026-11-05.
nodes.state: Data directory: release/<r>/ (stamps, unpacked tops), modules/, install targets and their .before-<r> copies.

nodes.cost: Z zip bytes, U unpacked bytes (OEWN 2025: 10 MB, 72 MB, 73 files): download O(Z), SHA-256 O(Z), unzip O(U), inventory SHA-256 O(U), load check parses every JSON file O(U) memory and time; about 0.6 s for check on the real data (2026-11-05).
nodes.description: `mova oewn`: Open English WordNet 2025 (JSON, CC BY 4.0) into $MOVA_DATA/raw/en-oewn/json: the zip's SHA-256, unpacking into staging, an exact inventory (tools/modules/oewn-2025-json.tsv, bound to the zip SHA-256) and a load check, then one rename; an installed folder is reused only when it passes the same checks.
forward: Inventory::parse reads `# zip-sha256 <hex>` and path/bytes/sha256 rows; oewn_2025 requires the header to equal ZIP_SHA256; check_dir requires exactly those regular files with those sizes and SHA-256.
check_load reads entries-*.json and the synset files as world::wordnet does and requires every file to be a JSON object, at least one sense, and every sense's synset present.

install reuses json/ if check_dir and check_load pass; otherwise takes the given zip, the kept zip with the right SHA-256 or downloads one (https or file://), checks its SHA-256, unzips into .json-staging-<pid>, checks both, renames to json/ (an earlier json/ kept as json.before-oewn-2025).
inverse: Behavior complement: no other editions or formats, no repair of a partial folder in place, no deletion of earlier folders or of the kept zip, no check of the meaning of the data beyond resolvable senses; staging folders of killed runs are left (never read).

Reverse reconstruction: a passing json/ conforms to the file inventory the compiled manifest associates with ZIP_SHA256; its contents alone do not reconstruct the zip bytes or establish their provenance; a downloaded zip is retained beside it, a supplied zip stays at its supplied path, and reuse of a valid folder needs no zip; an earlier folder survives as json.before-oewn-2025[-n]; the URL it came from is not recorded.
limitations: Partial source model; fixture zips (stored entries) in tests and the real OEWN 2025 folder checked on 2026-11-05.
nodes.state: Data directory: raw/en-oewn/ (the kept zip, json/, json.before-oewn-2025*, .json-staging-<pid> while running).

checks: undate REPO --dry-run twice with identical reports; per-file verify and second-run idempotence inside every run; dropped-line, changed-word, invented-line, date-left, hash-left, note-missing, History-not-last, rewrite-outside-selection, invented-refill and dated-refill negative controls
nodes.cost: One Git listing, one read of every tracked JSON file and every groupant model.md; per file a linear line scan plus O(L log L) multiset verification; hash rebinding rescans the JSON texts once per round until fixpoint (at most 16 rounds).
nodes.description: Undated main text for groupant model.md files: dated material and provenance live verbatim in one final ## History section; JSON-selected sections keep their current substance (dated sentences rewritten without dates, heading-only ones refilled from their newest History group); fresh hash-bound references are rebound.
forward: Parse unfenced ATX heading blocks and paragraph/list/table/record-line units; move dated or provenance units and dated heading blocks (not a section lead, not a JSON-selected H2) into ### <date> · <origin> History groups in chronological order; in a JSON-selected section a dated unit also stays, rewritten by strip_line; rename lead and H1 dated headings in place with a History note; refill every heading-only selected section from the newest History group of that origin that restates to a nonempty body; verify; rebind fresh path+sha256 JSON bindings to fixpoint; write unless --dry-run.
inverse: Never deletes a line; moved heading blocks change only their ATX level; rewritten or refilled lines appear only in selected sections and are strip_line images of verbatim History lines; no dated line or provenance stays outside History except JSON-selected H2 headings and fenced code; stale hashes are reported, never refreshed.

Each History line maps back to its origin section named in its group heading; a rewritten main-text line maps back to its History line through the many-to-one strip_line; original positions inside a section and blank-line spacing are not recoverable.
limitations: Date and provenance detection are lexical rules (ISO dates 2025-2029 with toolchain and data-snapshot exclusions; 40+ hex digests, abbreviated digests, $MOVA_DATA/ paths). strip_line removes date frames by fixed patterns. No semantic judgement of what is current; a refill takes only the newest restatable group, and an unselected section whose only text was dated is left empty.

checks: sidecar-links red on the tree before relink-evidence and green after it; relink-evidence --dry-run twice with identical reports; a second relink run rewrites nothing
nodes.cost: One Git listing, one git log of deleted paths, one read of every tracked Markdown and JSON file; per sidecar Markdown file a linear token scan with ordered-set lookups over at most depth+2 candidate directories; hash rebinding is the undate rebinder (at most 16 rounds over the JSON texts).
nodes.description: Dangling sidecar references: sidecar-links reports Markdown inside *.groupant/ that names an absent sibling or parent .md/.json file or an absent heading; relink-evidence rewrites former-file names to the model.md#section now holding their block and rebinds fresh hashes.
forward: Tokenize path-like .md/.json names (with #fragment) outside $-, ~-, URL- and glob-contexts; skip syntax.json, hash provenance records (name followed by its SHA-256) and bare names that neither exist nor existed in the sidecar chain; report absent files and absent heading anchors.

For a dangling name, try the former location from the writing sidecar, each enclosing sidecar and the source directory (a module prospective.md maps to mod.rs.groupant); the first former file in Git history whose sidecar model.md has an H2 with the stem's anchor gives model.md#anchor relative to the writer, else a History group named after the stem gives model.md#history; a whole link label becomes the heading name.
inverse: Behavior complement: never deletes files or lines, never changes text other than the dangling token, never invents a section (an unresolved name stays and is listed), never refreshes an already stale hash and never touches the external store.

Reverse reconstruction: each rewrite is listed with file, line, former token and new token, so the former text is recoverable from the report; without the report model.md#stem maps back to the set of former spellings (stem.md, ../stem.md, parent qualifiers), not to one.
limitations: Lexical scan, not Markdown rendering; a bare name that never existed in the chain is presumed external and not checked; prose qualifiers (parent, file-root) are left as written; path tokens are accepted when they resolve from any ancestor directory.
